_convention: Stance is favourability TOWARD THE THING `target` NAMES. Nothing else.
Every entry must carry a target, because an issue label that names an
event leaves the referent implicit, and getting it wrong does not blur a
score - it inverts it. 'Net zero rollback' is the worked example: the
Guardian is hostile to a rollback and the Express welcomes it, so an
instrument that reads the label as 'net zero' gets both papers backwards.
On a red-to-green globe an inverted issue is not slightly off, it is the
wrong colour.
`expect` records the polarity we believe holds, in plain words, before any
data is scored. Where the left/right ordering is genuinely not in doubt,
set regression:true and the direction test asserts the SIGN of the
left-minus-right difference on every scoring run. That catches an
inversion the day it appears rather than after a month of archive.
`expect` is a prior for testing, never an input to scoring. The scorer
must not see it. An issue where the data contradicts a non-regression
expectation is a finding, not a bug.
`includes` / `excludes` are the boundary, and they exist because the
classifier will otherwise drift: 'Energy bills' quietly absorbs 'Net zero'
over a winter unless told not to.
Changing this file changes the meaning of every score computed under it,
so bump `version`, never edit in place. A version change is a bounded
re-score of the archive, costed in the plan, not a tidy-up.

issues.name: Small boats & asylum
issues.target: people crossing the Channel in small boats, and asylum seekers in the UK

expect.why: the clearest left/right split in the British press

excludes: legal migration and visa numbers -> legal-migration
small boat deaths as a maritime rescue story only

issues.name: Legal migration & visas
issues.target: current levels of legal migration to the UK

expect.why: the left is split between labour-supply and restrictionist arguments

issues.name: NHS winter pressures
issues.target: the current state of the NHS

expect.why: everyone reports it badly; they disagree on the cause, not the state. Scoring blame would be a different measurement

issues.name: NHS pay & industrial action
issues.target: the pay claims of NHS staff, including strike action

expect.why: a straightforward industrial-action split

issues.name: Energy bills & cost of living
issues.target: the level of household energy bills and living costs

expect.why: no paper is in favour of high bills; the split is over who is blamed

issues.name: Autumn Budget & taxation
issues.target: the Budget's tax and spending decisions as announced

expect.why: depends entirely on the government of the day; do NOT regression-test this

issues.name: Interest rates & mortgages
issues.target: the current level of interest rates and mortgage costs

issues.name: Housing & planning reform
issues.target: building more homes, including planning reform to allow it

expect.why: the right splits between growth and green-belt defence, so this one genuinely moves

issues.name: Net zero rollback
issues.target: WEAKENING or delaying net zero commitments

expect.why: THE inversion case. The label names the rollback, not the policy. The Guardian opposes a rollback; the Express welcomes it. Read the wrong way round, this issue alone flips a quarter of the press map

excludes: energy bills as household cost -> energy-bills

issues.name: Climate impacts & storms
issues.target: the severity of extreme weather and its consequences in the UK

expect.why: shared alarm about the event; attribution to climate change is the contested part and is not what this measures

issues.name: Water companies & sewage
issues.target: the conduct of the privatised water companies

expect.why: rare cross-press hostility; the split is over remedy, not conduct

issues.name: Water bills
issues.target: increases in household water bills

issues.name: Knife crime & policing
issues.target: current levels of violent crime, and police effectiveness against it

expect.why: nobody is favourable to knife crime. The interesting axis here is salience, not stance

issues.name: Police vetting & standards
issues.target: the conduct and vetting standards of the police

issues.name: Prisons & sentencing
issues.target: shorter sentences and early release to relieve prison capacity

expect.why: the right is reliably hostile to early release; the left is split between reform and victim concern

issues.name: Grooming gangs inquiry
issues.target: a full national inquiry into grooming gangs

expect.why: the right campaigns for the inquiry; the left is warier of the framing. Note the target is the INQUIRY, not the crimes - nobody is favourable to those

issues.name: Ukraine
issues.target: continued UK military and financial support for Ukraine

expect.why: broad UK consensus, unlike the US press. Worth watching for divergence rather than assuming it

excludes: defence spending as a fiscal question -> budget-tax

issues.name: Middle East
issues.target: Israeli military action in Gaza and the wider region

expect.why: a real and stable split. The target must name whose action is being judged or this issue is meaningless

excludes: domestic protest and policing of it -> protest-policing

issues.name: Protest & public order
issues.target: the right to protest as currently exercised, including disruptive protest

expect.why: the target is the right to protest, not the cause being protested about - keep those apart or the sign follows whichever cause is in the news

issues.name: Reform UK's rise
issues.target: Reform UK's growing support

expect.why: a party-support target, reliably split

excludes: immigration policy itself -> small-boats or legal-migration

issues.name: AI and the jobs market
issues.target: the adoption of AI in the workplace

expect.why: business optimism against labour displacement; moves with the news

issues.name: AI in schools
issues.target: the use of AI by pupils and teachers in schools

issues.name: SEND & school funding
issues.target: the current funding of schools and SEND provision

issues.name: University funding
issues.target: the financial position of UK universities and remedies for it

expect.why: the right is hostile to bailouts and to the sector; the left more sympathetic, but this is softer than the regression cases

issues.name: Social care funding
issues.target: the current funding and staffing of adult social care

issues.name: NHS dentistry access
issues.target: the availability of NHS dentistry

issues.name: Council finances
issues.target: the financial position of local councils

issues.name: Pension triple lock
issues.target: keeping the state pension triple lock

expect.why: the right-leaning popular press defends it hard; the left is more willing to question it

issues.name: Farming & inheritance tax
issues.target: applying inheritance tax to farms

expect.why: another target-direction case: the label names the tax, and the right opposes it

issues.name: BBC licence fee
issues.target: keeping the licence fee as the BBC's funding model

expect.why: reliably split, and a useful check because the BBC scores itself here

excludes: BBC editorial rows unless about funding

issues.name: Channel 4's future
issues.target: privatising or restructuring Channel 4

expect.why: same shape as the licence fee but far lower volume, so noisier

issues.name: Assisted dying bill
issues.target: legalising assisted dying

expect.why: a conscience issue that cuts ACROSS the left/right axis. Valuable precisely because it should show a flat gradient - if it shows a steep one, the model is reading party lines into a free vote

issues.name: Post Office redress
issues.target: compensation and redress for wrongly convicted subpostmasters

expect.why: cross-press consensus; a good calibration control, since a model that manufactures a split here is over-reading

issues.name: Rail fares & services
issues.target: the cost and reliability of rail travel

issues.name: HS2 & rail investment
issues.target: continued investment in HS2 and major rail schemes

issues.name: Airport expansion
issues.target: expanding UK airport capacity

expect.why: a clean growth-versus-environment split

issues.name: Steel & heavy industry
issues.target: state support for UK steel and heavy industry

issues.name: Gambling reform
issues.target: tighter regulation of gambling

expect.why: cuts across: some right-leaning titles campaign hard on harm, others defend the industry and sport sponsorship

issues.name: Football governance
issues.target: independent regulation of English football

issues.name: The Royal family
issues.target: the Royal family as an institution and its senior members

expect.why: one of the few reliably POSITIVE targets on the right, which makes it a useful check that the scale is not stuck below zero

issues.name: Fishing quotas & access
issues.target: granting EU vessels access to UK fishing waters

expect.why: target-direction case again: the label must name ACCESS, or the sign is ambiguous

issues.name: UK-EU relations
issues.target: closer alignment between the UK and the EU

expect.why: the most durable axis in the British press
